body.statement: Theorem 2 strictly replaces the unknown-baseline promise of Proposition 10 in Squires et al. on the observed-coordinate fully covered perfect-intervention subclass: both two-node constructions are legal members of \(\mathcal M_2\), the first gives literal scores \((3,2,2)\) and symmetric scores \((3,3,4)\), the second gives symmetric scores \((3,2,3)\), and the legal three-node fork gives literal scores \((5,4,5,5)\); in each case the coordinate certificate returns the true baseline and explanation.
body.justification: Low-dimensional legal families locate the failed rank inequality and prevent the replacement theorem from being presented as a mere alternative algorithm.
body.gap: The published proposition asserts unique rank-score minimization; the displayed legal families falsify both its literal formula and the natural symmetric repair.
body.consumer: Users of the ICML reduction obtain a valid baseline preprocessing step and explicit regression tests for implementations.
body.proof_tex:
For the chain \(1\to2\) in
\(\texttt{def:two-node-counterfamilies}\), direct inversion, or the row
factorization \(K=A^{\top}\Omega^{-1}A\), gives
\[
 K_0=
 \begin{pmatrix}
 u^{-1}+b^2v^{-1}&-bv^{-1}\\
 -bv^{-1}&v^{-1}
 \end{pmatrix},\quad
 K_1=
 \begin{pmatrix}
 t^{-1}+b^2v^{-1}&-bv^{-1}\\
 -bv^{-1}&v^{-1}
 \end{pmatrix},\quad
 K_2=
 \begin{pmatrix}
 u^{-1}&0\\
 0&s^{-1}
 \end{pmatrix}.                                                    \tag{19}
\]
All five parameters are positive, \(b\neq0\), and the root intervention
is effective in each displayed specialization because \(t\neq u\).
Target \(2\) is nonroot, so its intervention is effective regardless of
whether its variance changes.  Thus both specializations are legal members
of \(\mathcal M_2\).

For \((b,u,v,t,s)=(2,1,1,3,2)\), (19) becomes
\[
 K_0=\begin{pmatrix}5&-2\\-2&1\end{pmatrix},\quad
 K_1=\begin{pmatrix}13/3&-2\\-2&1\end{pmatrix},\quad
 K_2=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&1/2\end{pmatrix}.
\]
The differences have ranks
\[
 R=\begin{pmatrix}0&1&2\\1&0&2\\2&2&0\end{pmatrix}.                \tag{20}
\]
Under the published restricted summation over component positions
\(1,2\), the scores are
\[
 (R_{01}+R_{02},\,R_{11}+R_{12},\,R_{21}+R_{22})=(3,2,2),
\]
whereas summing over every other component gives \((3,3,4)\).

For \((b,u,v,t,s)=(1,1,1,1/2,2)\), the precisions are
\[
 K_0=\begin{pmatrix}2&-1\\-1&1\end{pmatrix},\quad
 K_1=\begin{pmatrix}3&-1\\-1&1\end{pmatrix},\quad
 K_2=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&1/2\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Here
\[
 R=\begin{pmatrix}0&1&2\\1&0&1\\2&1&0\end{pmatrix},
\]
because \(K_1-K_2\) is nonzero with determinant zero.  The symmetric
scores are therefore \((3,2,3)\).

For the fork in \(\texttt{def:three-node-counterfamily}\), all noise and
intervention variances are positive, the root variance changes from \(1\)
to \(3\), and the two other targets are nonroots.  It is therefore legal.
Row-factorization gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 K_0&=\begin{pmatrix}14&-2&-3\\-2&1&0\\-3&0&1\end{pmatrix},&
 K_1&=\begin{pmatrix}40/3&-2&-3\\-2&1&0\\-3&0&1\end{pmatrix},\\
 K_2&=\begin{pmatrix}10&0&-3\\0&1/4&0\\-3&0&1\end{pmatrix},&
 K_3&=\begin{pmatrix}5&-2&0\\-2&1&0\\0&0&1/5\end{pmatrix}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Direct minors give the frozen rank matrix
\[
 R=\begin{pmatrix}
 0&1&2&2\\
 1&0&2&2\\
 2&2&0&3\\
 2&2&3&0
 \end{pmatrix};
\]
for example, the determinant of \(K_2-K_3\) is \(11/20\neq0\).
Summation over the published positions \(1,2,3\) gives
\[
 (5,4,5,5).
\]
Thus the first and third examples exclude the actual baseline from the
literal score minimizers, while the symmetric repair ties it in the first
example and excludes it in the second.  In every example,
\(\texttt{thm:complete-certificate}\) is complete and therefore accepts
the legal tuple, and its uniqueness conclusion returns the true baseline
and semantic explanation.  This supplies the asserted strict replacement
on the stated fully covered observed-coordinate subclass.
